solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exiled bishop disappeared scratching head

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: scratching out the head means the first letter of the word for disappeared is struck off

parts.note: disappeared means vanished

explanation.surface: A bishop sent into exile has vanished, leaving puzzled onlookers scratching their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: To be banished is to be expelled from one's country, which is what being exiled means.

clue.text: A sprinkler came into activity

parts.note: the rose is the perforated nozzle on a watering can that sprinkles the water

explanation.surface: A garden sprinkler suddenly springs into action.
explanation.walkthrough: A rose is the sprinkling head on a watering can or hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that arose came into being or started happening, as a problem arises.

clue.text: Youngster army trained, new soldier

parts.note: an infant is a very young child

indicators.note: letters trained into a new shape, so the word army is rearranged

explanation.surface: A young recruit is drilled by the army into a fresh soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman is a foot soldier serving in the infantry.

clue.text: Protective covers shielding road in excavation with stone coming up

indicators.note: the road sits in the middle of the ditch word

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch dug as a boundary in a landscaped garden

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Builders' helmets protect workers digging a trench by a road while stones fly up.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch used as a hidden boundary in English country gardens. 'coming up' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard hats are helmets worn on building sites to protect the head.

clue.text: Regional boss of detective, comparatively tough, catching guy with silver

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the stricter word catches the guy and silver inside it

parts.note: stricter means tougher, the comparative of strict
a guy is a man
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A local chief, a tough detective, nabs a man carrying silver.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, a Detective Inspector, is the usual crossword detective in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A district manager runs operations across one area, a boss for a region.

clue.text: Wild herb carpets outside of villa

indicators.note: to carpet is to cover, so the herb wraps around the other letters

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

indicators.note: the outside of villa is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An untamed herb spreads across the grounds around a villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpets' is a verb here: the herb covers the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and wild both describe untamed animals or fierce, uncivilised behaviour.

clue.text: Label with time passing becomes weaker

indicators.note: time passing means time goes away, so its letter is lost

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A label fades and grows weaker as time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from STICKER leaves the answer; 'becomes' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sicker is more ill, and so physically weaker.

clue.text: Endlessly wind angled object

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to wind, as a road winds, is to veer and turn

explanation.surface: A twisting wind blows endlessly around some angular object.
explanation.walkthrough: VEER loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A vee is the letter V or anything shaped like it, two lines meeting at an angle.

clue.text: Fruit not mature? Check, we're told

parts.note: green fruit is unripe

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: to gauge is to measure or check

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fruit is unripe and is told to check.
explanation.walkthrough: GAUGE said aloud sounds like GAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum.

clue.text: One has shot with iron between hands

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a go

indicators.note: the iron sits between the two hand letters

parts.note: left and right hands give L and R
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone plays a shot with an iron gripped between both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a golfer too: 'One has shot with iron' could be the definition, but GO and LFER come from 'shot' and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer is a person who plays golf, the one who takes shots with clubs called irons.

clue.text: Hid case of some diamonds on island

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another follows it
the case of a word is its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone hid a case of diamonds on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of some diamonds' reads as one phrase, but 'case of' acts on 'some' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it, so secreted means hid.

clue.text: Pronounced conceited streak

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the synonym is turned into a word of the same sound

parts.note: a conceited person is vain

explanation.surface: Someone has a marked streak of arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a streak or seam, as of ore in rock or a vein of humour.

clue.text: Controlling hens with grains scattered around

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are scattered about and reassembled

explanation.surface: A farmer controls the hens by scattering grain around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Harnessing a force means bringing it under control and putting it to use.

clue.text: Failing torch in smog faulty

indicators.note: faulty letters are wrongly put together, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A torch fails to work in the smog.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming is a fault or defect, a failing in someone's character.

clue.text: Choose to accept period in charge of musical show

indicators.note: the choosing word accepts the period inside it

parts.note: to opt is to choose
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone opts to take a role in charge of a musical production.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'of musical show', an adjective phrase matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic describes what belongs to opera, a show set to music.

clue.text: Manuscript pieces found under church in passage

indicators.note: the church and pieces are put inside the passage word

parts.note: a part is a passage, as of a book or music

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces go beneath church

parts.note: men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Fragments of manuscript are found below a church in an underground passage.
explanation.walkthrough: CHMEN goes inside PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin for writing, and by extension a document written on it.

clue.text: Fine book many regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter of book many is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A fine book that many people regularly overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignoring B, O, M, N from BOOKMANY keeps O, K, A, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is okay means it is all right, acceptable, fine.

clue.text: Review disrupted Malaysians after mother leaves

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
mother leaves means her letters are taken out of the fodder

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A review is upset by Malaysians after their mother departs.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove MA from MALAYSIANS to leave LAYSIANS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed examination or study, a review of something.

clue.text: Out of shape needing runs to be brought forward

indicators.note: the runs letter is moved further forward in the word

parts.note: form means shape
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sports player is out of shape and needs runs to get back.
explanation.walkthrough: In FORM the R moves forward ahead of the O. 'Out of shape' looks like one phrase but only 'Out of' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: From and out of both mark origin, as in made from wood or out of wood.

clue.text: Entertainer in street not alien in 1050

indicators.note: the inner letters go inside the numeral pair

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and L is 50

indicators.note: the alien letters are not included, so they are removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing letters
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A street entertainer, no alien, performing in the year 1050.
explanation.walkthrough: 1050 is not a date here but two Roman numerals side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval singer or musician, an entertainer of the time.

clue.text: I'm uncertain on second-class express to north Italian region

parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation
B is the second grade after A

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading the letters upward

parts.note: to air a view is to express it

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about catching a second-class express train up to northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to north' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, around Perugia.

clue.text: Great pub I recalled in mind, bar close to heart

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: I as a Roman numeral is one

indicators.note: bar means except, so a letter is barred from the word

parts.note: mental means of the mind, here taken as its stand-in

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A great pub that I remember, with its bar close to my heart.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE reversed gives ENO; MENTAL without T (the end of heart) gives MENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means remarkable or extraordinary, a stronger way of saying great.

clue.text: River crossed by unclothed local swimmer

indicators.note: the river letter runs across inside the other letters
with its outer covering stripped, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A local swimmer, naked, crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL unclothed is OCA, with R put in.
explanation.definitionFit: An orca, the killer whale, is a large marine mammal that swims.

clue.text: Inlet encloses tip of lugged bulb section

indicators.note: the inlet word wraps around the other letter

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered inlet of the sea

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An inlet where someone has lugged a bulb ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one segment of a garlic bulb.

clue.text: Nobbled gaoler receiving pressure; fellow's opening vault

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in the other letters
nobbled means tampered with, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bribed jailer takes pressure from a fellow prisoner opening a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobbled' (British slang for tampered with) rearranges GAOLER into LEAROG; P and F go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To leapfrog is to vault over something, or over someone bending down in the game.

clue.text: Pierre's wrong to skip meal

indicators.note: the wrong letters are skipped over, taken out of the name

parts.note: the name Pierre, the 's meaning has
to err is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Pierre is wrong to skip a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E, R, R in order from PIERRE, leaving P, I and the last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish that can make a meal, a pastry filled with meat or fruit.

clue.text: Maybe diamonds and gold interested chap

parts.note: diamonds are one example of a suit in cards
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Diamonds and gold are what an interested man brings when courting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds and gold' looks like gifts from a wooer; diamonds is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, a chap interested in her.

clue.text: Olympian great, he naturally boxes

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a box holds its contents

explanation.surface: A great Olympian boxer, naturally talented, takes to the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was one of the Olympian gods of Greek myth, goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Was monarch bearing son passive?

indicators.note: the reigning word carries the son inside it

parts.note: to reign is to rule as monarch
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A monarch who ruled with a son in tow: was the king merely passive?
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means accepting what cannot be changed, an unresisting, passive attitude.
